items.title: Louie Bellson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: We were roommates for three years in Tommy Dorsey’s band. ... I learned a lot rooming with Charlie. He taught me a lot about music

ctx.x: Did you give him like a week’s notice this time when you left?

Yeah, I gave him proper notice this time, yeah. I played it straight this time. And after that, Benny was kind of semi-retired then. He was going to go back to New York and not do too much, so that left an opening for me to join Tommy Dorsey in 1947. And that was a great experience, a wonderful band. He had people in there like Charlie Shavers the great trumpet player, Ziggy Elman was still in the band then, Paul Smith on piano, and Tommy himself was just superb you know. I stayed with him for three years, and…

of us said “we have a chance to join Duke Ellington’s band.” So he looked at us and hesitated for about fifteen seconds, then he said “take me with you.” I’ll never forget those words you know. But he was a great man. Harry was a great player and a sensational band besides you know. But I did get a chance to work with him for a while. And then of course after that, of course with Ellington, there are so many stories about that band, and Ellington himself was an element of surprise, always. Because you never knew…

items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Charlie Shavers was in Tommy’s band for three years too. We were roommates.

ctx.x: Do you want to talk about that period?

Charlie Shavers was in Tommy’s band for three years too. We were roommates. There was one of the greatest trumpet players that ever lived. Tommy Dorsey said he was – because he was not only a great trumpet player. He was a great piano player, great arranger, composer. Undecided. He wrote Undecided with the John Kirby Sextet: O’Neill Spencer, brushes . . .
Talk about O’Neill, because a lot of people don’t know about him.
